ORDER OF WORK
I did my own calculation first and only then read LAB.md items L4, L5, L13, L17 and the journal post-mortem line (journal.md line 556).

CALCULATION
- Inputs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/pm/trades.csv (byte-identical to /home/user/test-trading/trader/trades.csv) and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/pm/day_0908_1110.json.
- Per leg, exactly as specified: model = next open / entry-session close - 1; ours = exit fill / entry fill - 1; entry leg = close / entry fill - 1; exit leg = exit fill / open - 1. Dollars = entry fill x quantity x each term; cross = ours - model - entry - exit.
- Interpolated or zero-volume bars were skipped.
- Inference by night: each night's legs were summed in dollars and divided by that night's invested dollars. Percentile bootstrap over nights, 20,000 and 200,000 resamples.
- A second, separately written pass reproduced every total and interval.

OTHER FILES READ
- /home/user/test-trading/trader/orders.jsonl: intent lines matched to legs by date, symbol and E/X suffix.
- /home/user/test-trading/trader/RULES_v3.md sections 1 to 9, /home/user/test-trading/trader/LAB.md, /home/user/test-trading/trader/journal.md (lines 516-518, 539, 556), /home/user/test-trading/trader/report/DAY-20261110.md, /home/user/test-trading/trader/equity.csv, /home/user/test-trading/trader/research/EXEC-TIMING-20261021.md.
- To test the study's claim I also read its own scratch data, which was not on my list: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/exec_timing/tierA.csv, tierB.csv, m1.csv and s02_build.py. Reading only.

COMPARISON WITH LAB L4 AND THE JOURNAL
- Identical: -19.76 total, -9.49 model, -7.80 exit (0.205%), -2.85 entry (0.075%), "timing about -10.3" (= -7.80 - 2.85 + 0.38 cross), era figures +6.57 / +3.28 and -16.06 / -23.04, exit -0.37% in the NVDA era, N43 = 80% of the loss, -0.34% entry leg in November, and the context returns.
- Different, significance: the journal gives the NVDA-era exit leg "t -2.8, 29 legs" and L17 gives the entry leg "t -1.8 on 82 legs". Same-morning legs are one observation. By night these are t -2.0 (20 nights) and t -1.28 (44 nights).
- Different, night count: the journal's close-to-open figures for TQQQ, SOXL, UPRO and QQQ cover 43 nights, not 44, without saying so.
- Different, small sums: reports say campaign -19.79 (sum of rounded per-leg figures) against -19.764 from fills; the day leg is +3.24 from fills against the journal's +3.22.

Scripts and outputs are in the scratch directory: attr.py, nightly.py, gap.py, dq.py, limits.py, orders_match.py, context.py, study_check.py, recheck.py and the matching out_*.txt files. Nothing under /home/user/test-trading was created or changed (git status clean).
findings: (1) WHERE THE MONEY WENT. Of -$19.76, the market move of what was held is -$9.49 (48%), the exit leg -$7.80 (39%), the entry leg -$2.85 (14%), cross +$0.38. The market part is two nights: N43 -13.93 and N44 -4.01; the other 42 nights had a market move of +$8.44. The first era (nights 1-24) made +$3.28 on a +$6.57 model. The NVDA-only era (nights 25-44) lost -$23.04 on a -$16.06 model.

(1b) BEFORE THE CRASH THE STRATEGY WAS NOT EARNING EITHER. After 42 nights it was +$1.50: model +$8.44 less -$6.92 of timing (exit -4.23, entry -2.69). Measured timing cost is 0.28% of invested dollars per night over all 44 nights and 0.19% over the first 42. The rules' planning edge is +0.30% a night gross (RULES_v3.md section 3). At the measured cost the expected net edge is about zero even if the thesis is right.

(1c) THE RECORD CANNOT SHOW WHETHER AN EDGE EXISTS. Our nightly return has sd 4.04%, so the standard error of the 44-night mean is 0.61%; the 90% interval for the mean is -1.54% to +0.44%, which contains both zero and +0.30%. On a rough normal approximation a total this bad or worse is about a 1-in-5 draw for a zero-edge strategy at this volatility.

(2) BY-NIGHT INFERENCE. Exit leg: mean -0.210% of invested, 90% bootstrap interval -0.42% to 0.00%, 26 of 44 nights negative, sign test p 0.29. Entry leg: mean -0.083%, interval -0.185% to +0.025%, 26 of 44 negative. Neither excludes zero at the usual standard. The exit shortfall is not only the two crash mornings: the median night is -0.12%, the mean with the 2 best and 2 worst nights dropped is -0.21%, and each month is negative (Sep -0.16%, Oct -0.12%, Nov -0.62%). In the NVDA-only era the interval excludes zero (-0.70% to -0.09%) only because of the last two mornings; without them it is -0.45% to +0.05%.

(2b) THE TWO LEGS BELONG TO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS. The whole exit shortfall is in NVDA 2x legs: -$7.72 over 39 nights, mean -0.28% a night, t -2.1, 25 of 39 negative; the other names total -$0.08. Nearly the whole entry shortfall is in the retired names METU, AAPU and AMZU: -$2.67. For NVDL and NVDX the entry leg is -$0.19 over 39 nights (mean -0.016%, t -0.2). LAB L17's premise therefore has almost no support for the instrument now traded; the November figure of -0.34% is 6 nights.

(3) GAP DIRECTION AGAINST GAP SIZE. The exit shortfall follows the size of the overnight gap, not its direction. Night level: gap below -2%: -0.74% (10 nights, 7 negative); between: +0.10% (24 nights, 12 negative); above +2%: -0.43% (10 nights, 7 negative). Down nights -0.23% against up nights -0.18%. Big-gap nights (20) average -0.59% (t -3.0) against +0.10% on quiet ones. By era: nights 1-24: -0.96% (n=2), +0.20% (n=17), -0.59% (n=5, all negative); nights 25-44: -0.69% (n=8; -0.23% without N43 and N44), -0.125% (n=7, 6 negative), -0.27% (n=5). The correlation of exit leg with signed gap is +0.32 with the last two mornings and +0.07 without.

(3b) THE SIZE EFFECT IS NOT IN THE OLDER DATA. In the study's own 5-minute data for the 133 mornings from 2/23 to 9/4, the move from the open to 09:35 after an NVDL gap larger than 2% in either direction averaged +7bp (55 mornings). In the live window from 9/8 it was -66bp (17 mornings, t -2.7). I would treat the size effect as a feature of this window, not a rule.

(3c) THE LAST TWO MORNINGS WERE REAL MOVES IN NVDA. The journal's 09:31:05 quotes show NVDA about 0.9% below its own open one minute after the bell on both 11/9 and 11/10 (171.56 against 173.065; 172.35 against 173.97). Doubled, that is the -1.9% and -2.0% NVDL shortfall. It is not a bad open print or a fill problem. On 11/9 the 09:31 sale at 19.83 was near the day's low of 19.53; NVDL closed at 21.64.

(4) TRADE LOG AGAINST FILLS. The log's profit column sums to -15.69 because the column layout changed twice. Nights 1-7 (14 legs): that column holds profit as a percent of account equity (sums to -0.72 against -0.90 in dollars). Nights 8-11 (11 legs): it holds the leg's percent return (+6.46 against +2.54 in dollars). Nights 12-44 (57 legs): dollars (-21.43 against -21.41). The -19.76 from fills is the correct figure. Three percent entries on nights 34-35 are off by 0.03 to 0.16 points; their dollars are right.

(4b) COMPLETENESS. 44 night ids, one per session from 9/9 to 11/9, none missing, none duplicated, no repeated night-and-symbol pair. Every fill lies inside that session's high-low range. Starting equity 98.75 - 19.76 nights + 3.24 day leg = 82.22 against broker cash of 82.31 after the N44 exit. The $0.09 difference cannot be explained from the files I had.

(4c) ORDERS. All 82 entries and 82 exits have an intent line in orders.jsonl with the same quantity. Every buy filled at or under its limit. Every sell filled at or above the limit in force. Five legs on four mornings missed the first limit and were re-priced about 80 seconds later (N03 NVDL, N07 METU, N11 METU, N28 NVDL and NVDX); the re-price lines for N03 and N07 hold text, not a number. Small record errors: trades.csv says 09:31 for N11 METU though its re-price intent is stamped 09:32:49; the N09 entry intent is stamped 15:49:51; the exit intents for N12, N15, N16 and N17 are stamped 09:30:44 to 09:30:58, before the 09:31:05 rule time.

(4d) THE FILL AGAINST THE QUOTE IS NOT THE LEAK. I backed out the quoted bid from each exit limit (limit = bid - 0.15%). The exit leg of -$7.80 splits into -$8.26 of price movement from the open print to the 09:31:05 bid and +$0.46 of fill against that bid. This agrees with LAB L13 (fills average 23bp above the limit; I get 22.7bp).

(4e) L13 WAS CLOSED ON AN AVERAGE THAT HIDES A RECENT CHANGE. Sells filling at the limit to the cent: 15 of the first 72 legs, then 8 of the last 10 (nights 36-44, 7 of 9 mornings). At the earlier rate that has a chance of about 1 in 10,000. Three of those mornings (N38, N40, N42) were mornings when the price one minute in was above the open. If each such fill gave up the full 0.15%, the cost for nights 36-44 is at most $0.93. Whether the bid had really fallen each time cannot be determined from these files.

(4f) THE BENCHMARK IS SLIGHTLY GENEROUS. On the 31 mornings where the study has 1-minute bars, the day-bar open is on average 5bp above the first print of the 09:30 minute bar (NVDL -4.7bp, t -2.8; NVDX -5.1bp), and it lies outside that minute's range on 9 of 64 symbol-mornings. Measured against the minute-bar open, the NVDA 2x exit leg on those mornings is -19.8bp by night instead of -23.0bp. An order aimed at the open will not necessarily get the day-bar open.

(5) WHAT THE STUDY ACTUALLY MEASURED. Its 09:31:05 price for the 164 mornings is a formula: open + 21.7% of the move from the open to the 09:35 close (s02_build.py line 56). It cannot sit far from the open by construction. Its headline (open print 0.6bp worse) is the statement that the open-to-09:35 move averaged +3.0bp (sd 127bp, t 0.3); I reproduced that from tierA.csv. On the 32 mornings with real 1-minute bars (9/8 to 10/21) the move from the open to the 09:31 minute averaged -18.7bp (t -1.6) while the formula read -3.9bp. The study is weaker evidence about the first minute than its summary suggests.

(5b) NOISE OR A REAL CHANGE. The live numbers are consistent with noise around a small steady cost. In like-for-like data the 133 earlier mornings show +8bp from open to 09:35 and the 31 live-window mornings -19bp; the difference is t -1.2. October 1-20 alone is -49bp (t -2.25, 14 mornings), one month of nine. After the study, the 12 exits from 10/22 to 11/6 averaged -0.09% (t -0.5), then came -2.03% and -2.14%. With no drift at all I would still expect about -5 to -10bp a night: we sell at the bid (half the spread, 3-5bp), the day-bar open is about 5bp above the first tape print, and there are occasional re-prices. A real change can be neither shown nor ruled out: the standard error on 44 nights is 13bp.

(5c) PROBABILITY FOR THE NEXT 44 NIGHTS. I give about 70% (range 60-80%) that the official opening print would beat the 09:31:05 fill in total. Reasons: a believable true mean of about -10bp (structural cost plus part of the live -21bp), uncertainty of about 8bp on that mean, and 13bp of sampling noise over 44 nights. The expected advantage is about 10bp a night: roughly 2 cents a night at one share, or $3-4 per 44 nights at about $80 invested. I give about 25% that the advantage is as large as the live 20bp a night. This assumes the opening print can actually be obtained; whether this broker fills at the auction price cannot be determined from the data.

(6) CONTEXT. Close-to-open over the same nights, compounded, price only: NVDL -7.10% (mean -0.085% a night, sd 4.05%, 22 of 44 up; +16.3% without its two worst nights), NVDX -7.02%, NVDA -1.16%; over 43 nights TQQQ -6.77%, QQQ -1.15%, SOXL -36.20%, UPRO +7.26%. Buy and hold from the 9/9 close to the 11/10 close: NVDL -45.74%, NVDA -24.49%. To the 11/9 close: TQQQ -19.52%, QQQ -5.16%, SOXL -55.35%, UPRO -6.30%. NVDL's open-to-close moves compounded to -37.86%, so being in cash by day avoided a far larger loss. But the overnight half was itself negative: the thesis held in relative terms and there was no positive return to collect.
caveats: 44 nights is a small sample with two extreme observations. The bootstrap intervals are by night but still rest on those 44 values; the upper end of the exit-leg interval sits at zero and moves by a few thousandths of a percent between runs.

The gap-size split, the era split, the month split and the NVDA-only split are several cuts of the same 44 nights. The big-gap result (t -3.0) is not corrected for that and did not appear in the 133 earlier mornings.

The 'official open' is the broker day bar's open. On overlapping mornings it averages about 5bp above the first 1-minute print and is sometimes outside that minute's range. I cannot tell from the files which print an order placed for the open would receive.

Close-to-open returns for TQQQ, QQQ, SOXL and UPRO cover 43 nights: their 11/10 bars in the file are zero-volume placeholders, so night 44 and buy-and-hold to 11/10 cannot be determined for them. The NVDL and NVDA 11/10 closes are the latest bar's close, which the data guide says is not the settled official close.

Prices are split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted. Any distribution on METU, AAPU, AMZU, QQQ, TQQQ, SOXL or UPRO in the window would make that night's close-to-open figure slightly too low. I could not check ex-dates.

The quoted bid at 09:31:05 is inferred from the logged limit (limit = bid - 0.15%), accurate to about one cent. The actual quotes sit in the journal's shadow lines, which I checked only for N43 and N44 (both agree).
The $0.09 gap between trade-log arithmetic and broker cash is unexplained. I had no access to broker records.
The at-limit fill pattern since 10/29 cannot be resolved without broker order timestamps and quotes at execution. The $0.93 figure is an upper bound, not a measured loss.

The 70% probability is a judgement built from a normal approximation and a prior taken from the study's earlier mornings. It is not a measured frequency. The roughly 1-in-5 figure for a zero-edge strategy is the same kind of approximation and uses a volatility that includes the two crash nights.
The study's scratch files under scratchpad/exec_timing were not on my list of data. I read them to test the study's claim and did not re-verify how they were pulled from the broker.
reports.recommendation:
For the owner, the plain answer: the account lost because it held nearly all its money in a 2x single-stock fund through two nights when that stock fell (11/6 to 11/9 and 11/9 to 11/10: -$21.27, more than the whole campaign loss), and because in the 42 nights before that, buying a little above the close and selling below the open had already used up about $6.90 of an $8.44 market gain. There is no evidence in these 44 nights of an edge after costs, and none of a timing change that would have made the strategy profitable.

For the lab:
1. Do not expect the L4 open-print pilot to recover the loss. The repeatable part of the -$7.80 is probably about 10bp a night, which is 2 cents a night at one share. If it runs, judge it by night, not by leg, and record the first 1-minute print as well as the day-bar open, because they differ by about 5bp.
2. Lower the priority of L17. For NVDL and NVDX the entry leg is -$0.19 over 39 nights; the 0.075% figure comes from names no longer traded.
3. Correct the stated significance in LAB L4, L17 and the journal to by-night values (exit leg in the NVDA era t -2.0 on 20 nights; entry leg t -1.3 on 44 nights), and note that the index context figures cover 43 nights.
4. Reopen L13 for the mornings since 10/29 only. Eight of the last ten sells filled at the limit to the cent, against 15 of the first 72. It needs broker order timestamps, which I did not have.
5. Do not sum the profit column of trades.csv until nights 1-11 are put in the same layout as the rest; use fills.
6. The dollars are in position risk, not execution: two nights account for 108% of the loss. That is the question L5 and sizing address, and it deserves more attention than exit timing. I did not test any alternative and make no claim that one would have done better.

reports.headline: L5 fails its pre-registered criteria: keep NVDL only, do not propose the 50/50 split with TQQQ. Over 2015 to 2026-11-06 the split gave up 0.069% (2015-20) and 0.121% (2021-26) of compound growth a night against an allowance of 0.010%; its worst night and worst drawdown were marginally worse than NVDL-only in 2015-20 (the March 2020 crash hit TQQQ as hard as 2x NVIDIA); and it did not lower the KILL probability (1.1% against 1.2%, a tie). It did cut volatility by about a quarter and PAUSE triggers by about a third. This is a verdict on risk and growth in past data, not a fix for the losses: over the 43 live nights that have both bars, TQQQ's close-to-open return was worse than NVDL's (-6.8% against -2.0% compounded).

reports.recommendation:
Keep NVDL only. Record L5 in the ledger as rejected, with the variant count from the method section, and do not test other weights: that would be a search after a failed pre-registered test.

What to tell the owner, plainly:
1. Splitting with TQQQ would not have stopped the losses. This autumn TQQQ's overnight return was worse than NVDL's, and across the live window a 50/50 mix at official prices would have lost about 2 dollars more than NVDL alone. It would have helped on one night (N43, about 8 dollars less) and hurt on others.
2. In 12 years of data the split is a risk trade, not an improvement. It cut volatility by about 25% and PAUSE triggers by about a third. It cost about 40% of the compound growth, was no better in a market crash, and left the chance of reaching the KILL level unchanged.
3. The one large loss came at full size the session before the trend rule took effect. That rule would have held a quarter position that night. The size rules already in force (trend size, PAUSE) do more against a night like N43 than a second fund does, and they do it without adding 3x index exposure.
4. Nothing in this test shows an edge that would make the account profitable. NVDL-only looks best only on the assumption that NVIDIA's past overnight premium persists; if it has dropped to the index's level, the split would be the sounder choice, and 44 nights cannot settle that.

If single-night loss matters more to the owner than growth, the lever the data supports is a smaller position, not TQQQ. The half-NVDL, half-cash benchmark had nearly the split's growth with a -13.9% worst night and a -34.7% worst drawdown. It was not pre-registered and gives up the same growth as the split, so it would need its own criteria and an independent run before anyone proposes it. The quarterly review on 2027-01-11 can revisit single-name risk with more live nights.

findings: (1) ROUTING AT THE OPEN IS NOT SETTLED BY PUBLIC SOURCES. Robinhood sends essentially all equity orders to wholesalers; no exchange appears as a venue in its Rule 606 reports (https://cdn.finra.org/606/2026/287900_606_NMS_2026_Q2_V1.pdf ; https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/RHS%20SEC%20Rule%20606%20and%20607%20Disclosure.pdf ; https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/stock-order-routing). Whether the wholesaler enters a queued order into Nasdaq's opening cross is not disclosed. Two Robinhood documents point in different directions. (a) The help page: a regular-hours order (good-for-day or good-til-canceled) in a NASDAQ-listed stock that you try to cancel or replace between 9:25 and 9:30 AM ET is kept pending 'until the opening cross for the stock', described as 'a NASDAQ rule that we can't change'; cancel before 9:25 'to avoid an execution' (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/cancel-a-pending-order/, Reference No. 4207919). That matches Nasdaq's own FAQ 25, 'Orders can be modified or cancelled for the opening cross prior to 9:25 a.m.' (https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/content/productsservices/trading/crosses/openclose_faqs.pdf), and implies cross participation. (b) The Customer Agreement, section 10: 'orders based on Queued Orders are sent out for execution after the opening of the normal market trading session' (https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/Robinhood-Customer-Agreement.pdf, revised 2026-11-02). NVDL is Nasdaq-listed (https://www.schwab.wallst.com/Prospect/Research/etfs/summary.asp?symbol=nvdl).

(1, continued) WHAT NASDAQ ALLOWS, AND THE PRICE AND DELAY TO EXPECT. Nasdaq FAQ 10: regular-hours DAY, GTC and market orders are executable 'including during the Cross'; 'Market Orders placed after 9:28 a.m. will be held until the market opens and will not participate in the Opening Cross'. FAQ 22: only interest on the Nasdaq book takes part. FAQ 5 and 6: the cross runs at 9:30:00 and sets the Nasdaq Official Opening Price; with no cross, the official open is the first last-sale-eligible trade. FAQ 3 and 4: for exchange-traded products the cross price must lie within the greater of 5% or $0.50 of the Nasdaq inside. So there are two possible outcomes. If the order is in the cross, it fills at 09:30:00 at the official opening price; in 10 shadow mornings that price was within about 16bp of the 09:29 bid. If it is released after the open, it fills some seconds after 09:30:00 at about the best bid of that moment, when spreads are widest; Robinhood warns that high volume at the open 'may cause delays in execution and executions at prices significantly away from the market price quoted' (https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/rhf-rhs-market-volatility-overview.pdf). A regular-hours marketable limit placed before the open sits in the same queue, with its limit as a floor. An order placed after 09:25 has no documented handling and may miss the cross.

(1, continued) NO COLLAR ON EQUITY MARKET ORDERS IS DOCUMENTED. Customer Agreement section 10: 'If you place a market order (irrespective of when you place it), you agree to pay or receive the prevailing market price at the time your market order is executed'. The market-order article mentions 5% only as a buying-power over-reserve for queued market buys and a 95% cap on dollar-based sells, not a price limit; it adds 'Orders held or placed during a halt or a closed market may fill at a very different price when trading resumes' (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/market-order-update). The 1% and 5% collars on Robinhood's site are for crypto. The app's 'limit order with a preset limit price' 2% from the last trade is a separate limit-order type (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/limit-order). Third-party claims of a 5% stock collar are unverified. A queued market sell must be treated as having no price floor.

(2) WHAT CAN GO WRONG FOR A SELL QUEUED FOR THE OPEN. (a) Cancel lock: no cancel takes effect from 09:25 to the cross; fractional queued orders lock from 09:20; 'During a trading halt, cancel requests aren't processed until the halt lifts' (cancel page above). (b) Delayed open or halt: Robinhood says delayed opens are 'most common for NYSE symbols' (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/why-hasnt-my-order-been-filled/); NVDL opens electronically on Nasdaq at 09:30:00, but after a regulatory or market-wide halt the queued order waits for the reopening, where a market order has no protection and a limit keeps its floor. Whether NVDL is halted when NVDA is halted I could not determine. (c) Limit-up-limit-down pause: bands exist only from 09:30, and the first reference price is the primary market's opening price, so the cross itself cannot be paused. All leveraged products are Tier 2 with a 10% band above $3 (https://cdn.luldplan.com/reports/LULD-2025-Annual-Report.pdf), multiplied by the leverage ratio per the Plan text quoted in SEC release 34-69062 (https://www.sec.gov/file/release-no-34-69062, read as a search extract), so 20% for NVDL. The open doubling was removed in 2020 (https://www.cboe.com/document/tech-spec/content/technical-specifications/cboe-limit-updown-faq/luld-amendment-18-update). An order filled at 09:30:00 escapes a first-minute pause that would block the present 09:31:05 exit for 5 to 10 minutes. (d) Opening print far from the pre-market quote: the 09:25 quote is poor (median spread 77bp; the open was up to 1.0% below and 2.3% above the 09:25 bid), and the cross may print up to 5% outside the Nasdaq inside. (e) Partial fill: impossible on 1 share; at larger size an order priced exactly at the cross price can be partly filled. (f) Rejection or cancellation by the broker ('Robinhood may in its discretion cancel any open orders', Customer Agreement section 10), or an order held for approval if trade approvals were on; they are off per state.json.

(2, continued) WORST CASE AGAINST THE PRESENT PROCEDURE. The present procedure quotes at 09:31:05, fills at about 09:31:25 at bid minus 0.15%, then bid minus 0.3%, then a market order by about 09:33. A queued LIMIT sell with floor L has three outcomes. Filled at the open: the difference is the price move from 09:30:00 to about 09:31:25, which is noise with sd of about 0.85 to 0.95% ($0.16 to $0.18 on one share); worst seen against the open sale in 38 NVDL mornings is 1.47% ($0.28); in a bad-print case it is bounded by the 09:31 price minus L, roughly $0.40 to $0.60. Open below L: the order rests, and the fallback is cancel, confirm, then the unchanged section 5 ladder, about 10 to 30 seconds later than now. Halt: both procedures are stuck; the limit still holds. A queued MARKET sell adds an unbounded bad-print or post-halt fill; I do not recommend it even for one share. A real benefit: a queued order still sells if the 09:26 wake is late, which happened on 10/30 and 11/2 (journal.md).

(3) ENTRY: SESSIONS AND FILLS. Robinhood extended hours are 7:00 to 9:30 AM and 4:00 to 8:00 PM ET; 'Our venues don't support market orders during extended or overnight trading'; a good-for-day extended-hours limit lives until the end of the last extended session that day (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/extendedhours-trading/). The 24 Hour Market is whole-share limit orders only (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/24hour-market). An extended-hours limit sent at 16:00:05 to 16:01 can fill at once if it is marketable; the same wholesalers take extended-hours flow (the 606 report shows payment of 9% of the spread from 4:00 to 8:00 PM). It is not guaranteed: 'orders may not fill or have limited tradability due to lower volume and wider price spreads'. This account has never had an extended-hours fill; capabilities.json records only orders placed and cancelled. NVDL quotes just after the close in the journal: 19.35/19.37 at 16:01 on 11/10 (10bp), 22.72/22.73 on 11/5 (4bp), 29.67/29.69 on 11/3 (7bp), 30.88/30.96 on 10/29 (26bp, an earnings evening). EXEC-TIMING measured 16:05 at -4.3bp against 15:52, not significant.

(3, continued) IS A 15:59:30 REGULAR-HOURS LIMIT A SAFER EQUIVALENT? Mechanically yes: it is the same marketable limit as now, filled in continuous trading at about the ask, and it does not join the closing cross (Robinhood offers no on-close order; Nasdaq's market-on-close cutoff is 15:55). But it removes the 15:55 re-price and the 15:58 cancel, leaves under 30 seconds, and cannot be followed by the fractional top-up, which is a regular-hours market order to be sent by 15:58 after the core fills. The official close of a Nasdaq-listed product with no closing cross is a time-weighted NBBO midpoint over 15:58:00 to 15:59:55 (Nasdaq FAQ 9), so 'the close' is partly a midpoint that a buyer cannot trade at. The prize is not there on NVDL: entries are +2.7bp above the close (t 0.34, 38 legs). The -2.85 'entry timing' loss is mostly METU (-2.32), which is no longer traded.

(3, continued) DAY-TRADE AND SETTLEMENT RULES. A buy from 16:00 to 20:00 keeps that day's trade date: the Customer Agreement moves only executions 'between 8 p.m. and 12 a.m. ET' to the following trading day. So buying at 16:00:05 and selling at the next open is not a same-day round trip. A 24-hour-market buy after 20:00 would share the trade date with the morning sale; never use all_day_hours for the entry. Separately, FINRA replaced the pattern-day-trader rules with intraday margin standards effective 2026-06-04, deleting the day-trade count and the $25,000 minimum, with a phase-in to 2027-10-20 (https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/notices/26-10). Robinhood states 'No more day trade restrictions or day trade calls with your Robinhood margin account' and that the $2,000 margin minimum still applies (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/pattern-day-trading/). RULES_v3 sections 1, 7 and 11 still budget '3 day trades per rolling 5 business days'; that text looks out of date, but no public page says how a limited-margin agentic account under $2,000 is treated, so it must be confirmed with the broker before anyone relies on it. Good-faith and free-riding violations are cash-account concepts: Robinhood says margin accounts 'Trade with unsettled funds from stock and option sales' and cash accounts cannot (https://robinhood.com/us/en/support/articles/robinhood-accounts). The account is type limited_margin and has reused same-day proceeds for 44 nights without a restriction. Neither change alters that pattern.

(4) LEVERAGED-ETF POINTS THAT MATTER. (a) NVDL's 20% band means NVDL itself rarely pauses, but NVDA (Tier 1, 5% band) can pause while NVDL keeps trading on wide quotes; a 09:30:00 fill avoids that window, a 09:31 exit does not. (b) Fractional NVDL orders are market-only, regular-hours-only, and cannot be cancelled from 09:20 to 09:30, so any open-order pilot must be whole shares; a fractional remainder stays on the section 5 market sell. (c) Robinhood labels leveraged and inverse products as complex, and the Customer Agreement has the customer acknowledge their risks (https://cdn.robinhood.com/assets/robinhood/legal/RHF%20ETP%20Disclosure.pdf ; info-labels article seen only as a search result). A review call can therefore return an information alert; 44 nights of NVDL orders went through without one blocking. (d) I found no Robinhood page restricting NVDL by session; the repository records it as tradable in all sessions. (e) Higher margin maintenance on leveraged products is irrelevant here because nothing is borrowed.

PILOT (X), ONE SHARE: SCOPE AND ORDER. Scope: only mornings when the whole position is exactly 1 whole NVDL share (the PAUSE exits of 11/11, 11/12, 11/13, 11/16 and 11/17), trade approvals off, no halt or news-pending flag on NVDL or NVDA, and not a crash-open morning (NVDA indicated at -5% or worse, or QQQ at -3% or worse), which stays clean for shadow L8. Steps, all times ET: (1) 07:45 wake: confirm position 1.000000, 0 open orders, approvals off; run review_equity_order once with an indicative limit and log the full response. (2) 09:21:00: quote NVDL bid, ask, last and timestamps. Skip the pilot and run section 5 unchanged if the bid is missing, the quoted spread exceeds 3% of the mid, or the quote is older than 60 seconds. (3) L = 0.98 x bid, rounded down to the cent. Robinhood's own preset collar for sells is 2% below the last trade, so this should not trip a price check. (4) 09:21:30: review_equity_order with the exact order: sell 1 NVDL, type limit, limit L, good-for-day, regular_hours. Any alert needing acknowledgement, or any sign of conversion or another session: do not send. (5) 09:22:00, hard deadline 09:24:00: write the intent line (new coid suffix, for example -XO), then place the same order. If the deadline is missed, place no pilot order that morning. (6) 09:24:30: read the order; it must be accepted and not terminal. Send no cancel after 09:24:59. The 09:25 and 09:29 shadow quotes continue.

PILOT (X): AFTER THE OPEN AND FALLBACK. (7) Read the order at 09:30:10, 09:30:20 and 09:30:40. (8) If filled: verify 0 positions and 0 open orders, then at 09:31:05 take the usual quote as the counterfactual and place NO order. (9) If not filled at 09:31:05: take the 09:31:05 quote; cancel; poll until the state is cancelled (never two live orders on a symbol); re-read the position. If the share is still held, run the section 5 ladder exactly as written, with a fresh quote if the cancel took more than 10 seconds. If the order filled during the cancel, stop there. If the cancel is not confirmed, keep polling and never send a second sell; alert the human at 09:33. Keep 09:22 as the fixed placement time. If the first two fills are not at the official open, move placement to 09:10 for the next two, changing nothing else.

PILOT (X): STOP CONDITIONS, RECORDS AND WHAT IT CAN SHOW. Stop the pilot and report after any of: order rejected or failed, or an acknowledgement-required alert; a fill more than 1% below the official open; a fill before 09:30:00; no fill although the official open was at least L + $0.01; cancel not confirmed within 30 seconds, or the share still unsold at 09:33:30; cumulative (pilot fill minus 09:31:05 bid) at or below -$1.50, which has about a 5% chance of triggering falsely over 20 mornings if the true difference is zero. L4 as written stops at 'unsold at 09:32', but the unmodified section 5 ladder can itself run past 09:32 (it filled at 09:31:54 on 11/5), so the lab should reword that line before the first order. Record each morning: 09:21 bid, ask, last and timestamps; L; both review responses; intent and submit times; order id; state at 09:24:30; 09:25, 09:29 and 09:29:50 quotes; order states at 09:30:10, :20 and :40; execution timestamp to the millisecond and price; official open from the day bar; the 09:30 and 09:31 one-minute bars; the 09:31:05 bid and ask; fill minus official open; fill minus 09:31:05 bid; fill minus the 09:31 bar average of open, high, low and close; seconds from 09:30:00 to execution; fallback used and cancel latency; running dollar totals. Reading the mechanics: a fill by 09:30:02 at the official open to the cent on every filled morning means cross-price execution; a later time or a different price means routing after the open. Five one-share mornings can answer that. They cannot show that the open is a better price: with an sd near 90bp, 20 mornings give a standard error of about 20bp against a claimed 30 to 37bp.

PROPOSAL (E), NOT FOR IMMEDIATE USE. Step 1, shadow only, at least 20 evenings: log the 15:52 fill, the 15:59:30 bid and ask, the official close, and the post-market bid, ask and last at 16:00:30 and 16:01:00. Step 2, only if the existing section 3(g) test is ever met (at least 120 new nights with a 15:52-to-close drift beyond 10bp and t at least 2.5), and only on one-share nights with no top-up. Variant A, preferred: at 15:59:30 a regular-hours good-for-day limit buy at ask + max(0.02, 0.15%), capped at last x 1.004; poll at 15:59:40 and 15:59:50; at 16:00:05 confirm it is filled or dead and cancel if still open. Variant B, post-close: at 16:00:20 quote; require a spread of at most 0.25%; run review_equity_order; place a limit buy at the ask, good-for-day, market_hours extended_hours, never all_day_hours; poll for 10 seconds; at 16:01:00 cancel, confirm, and re-price once; at 16:02:00 cancel, confirm cancelled and skip the night. An uncancelled order would stay live until 20:00. Known costs: no re-price loop, no fractional top-up after 16:00, and a skipped night forfeits a return with an sd of several percent to chase a few basis points.
caveats: I was barred from the broker tools, so I did not inspect the order tool's parameter names, the order-state names, or what review_equity_order returns for a pre-open regular-hours limit sell. The pilot steps assume the fields seen in orders.jsonl (type, limit, tif gfd, hours regular_hours); the first review call must confirm them.
Running the pilot needs a small, reviewed variant of the exit tool: exit_ovn.py computes bid minus 0.15%, not 0.98 x bid, and has no pilot intent label. I wrote nothing in the repository.

The central routing question rests on two Robinhood texts that conflict and on general Nasdaq rules. Wholesaler handling of queued retail orders is not public. Help-page quotes were extracted by a summarising fetch tool; the Customer Agreement, Rule 606, Nasdaq and limit-up-limit-down texts I read directly from the PDFs.

Some sources were not read first-hand. The leveraged-product band multiplier (10% x 2 = 20%) comes from a search extract of the SEC release, not the Plan text. The FINRA Rule 6320B page did not contain the trade-date wording a search summary attributed to it, so the same-day trade date for 16:00 to 20:00 fills rests on the Customer Agreement's 8 PM clause by implication. Regulator pages on good-faith and free-riding violations returned errors (404 and 403), so that point rests on Robinhood's accounts page and 44 nights of account history.

'Limited margin' is the broker interface's account type; no public Robinhood page defines it for an individual or agentic account. How the June 2026 day-trade change and the $2,000 minimum apply to this $82 account cannot be determined from public sources.
The shadow table uses quotes transcribed from journal lines. Four mornings give the 09:25 and 09:29 bids only as basis-point differences, so the 09:25 and 09:29 statistics use 10 of 14 mornings.

Official open and close are the broker's day bars, as the task instructs. I could not verify that the day-bar open equals the Nasdaq cross price on every date, nor that NVDL has an opening cross every day.

The -30bp exit gap on NVDL legs is a subset picked after the fact. All 82 legs give -12.9bp (t -1.0) and the independent 164-morning study gave -0.6bp. It may be a feature of the falling market of the last weeks; 79% of the 14-morning shadow total comes from 11/9 and 11/10.

My recompute of the exit gap is -7.29 dollars against -7.80 in LAB.md item L4. The ledger's three components (-9.49, -7.80, -2.85) sum to -20.14, not -19.76; mine (-9.61, -7.29, -2.85) sum to -19.75. The attribution re-derivation should reconcile this.
Post-close NVDL liquidity is judged from four journal quotes and the earlier study, not from a systematic sample.

SIZE OF THE PRIZE
- The exit shortfall is -0.21% a night (t -1.6). For NVDA-2x legs it is -0.28% (t -2.1), or -0.185% (t -1.5) without the last two mornings.

- A repeatable part of 0 to 10bp is plausible: the half-spread, and a day-bar open that the attribution report puts about 5bp above the first one-minute print.
- If the broker releases queued orders after the open instead of into the cross, the order sells at the first bid of the day, when the spread is widest. The sign can then be negative.
- So: -10bp to +10bp. That is -2 to +2 cents a morning on one share, -0.4 to +0.4 dollars a month. At full size, -1.7 to +1.7 dollars a month.

- A new order path, a new 09:21 wake, no cancel from 09:25 to 09:30, and a cancel-then-fallback sequence.
- The money at risk on one share is cents. The real risk is operator error.
- In five mornings it can show one thing: whether a queued limit order fills at 09:30:00 at the official open.
- Its one practical benefit: a queued order still exits when the wake is late, as on 10/30 and 11/2.

- Section 3(g) already fixed the test for this hypothesis, and it is not met (n 14, +35bp, t 1.35).
- L4 replaces it with 'not worse on average over 20 mornings', which a zero effect passes half the time.
- Section 14 says the lab places no orders and allows one rule change a week.

- Use the mechanics analyst's stop conditions.
- Judge adoption on mechanics alone with no price claim, or on the section 3(g) bar, counted by night.
